en: The national flower, sampaguita, releases its strongest fragrance at night to attract moth pollinators.
National Scientist Ramon Barba discovered that spraying potassium nitrate induces mango trees to flower out of season.
The Ifugao rice terraces utilize a traditional gravity-fed irrigation system channeling water directly from protected mountain forests.
Lucban's Pahiyas Festival celebrates the rice harvest by decorating houses with colorful, leaf-shaped rice dough called kiping.
The Philippine tarsier has enormous eyes that are actually larger than its brain to see insects in the dark.
Mount Mayon is classified as a perfect stratovolcano because its steep, symmetrical cone is formed by alternating layers of lava and ash.
The T'boli people weave the traditional T'nalak cloth using fibers extracted from the leaf stalks of the abaca plant.
The national gem, the Philippine pearl, is formed when a giant pearl oyster coats an irritant with nacre.
Traditional bahay kubo houses use elevated bamboo floors and woven nipa palm walls to maximize airflow during hot summers.
National Scientist Angel Alcala pioneered the use of coral reef transplantation to restore damaged marine ecosystems in the Philippines.
The Philippine Constitution mandates the state to protect the people's right to a balanced and healthful ecology.
Baguio's Panagbenga Festival celebrates the blooming of seasonal flowers that thrive in the city's cool, high-altitude climate.
